why: The figures README.md publishes between the canonical-bench markers, held as data so tools/check_canonical_benchmarks.py can detect drift. Re-measuring the canonical host needs that host; noticing that a published number changed does not. Editing a figure in README.md without editing it here fails the gate, and so does adding one that cites no source.

canonical-bench-host.description: Linux x86-64 with AVX-512F/VL/BW/DQ/VBMI + VAES + VPCLMULQDQ (Sapphire Rapids / Zen 4 class), Python 3.11.15, native C backend via ctypes. Not a runner this project's CI has.

sandbox-host.description: The secp256k1 fixed-base comb measurement host, raw C, reported alongside the Welch t-test in docs/BENCHMARK_HISTORY.md.

comb-table-size.description: Not a measurement of a machine: the 4-block fixed-base comb table is a compile-time constant, 16 entries, sized from the generator table in src/c/ama_secp256k1.c.
comb-table-size.command: sizeof the comb table in src/c/ama_secp256k1.c

literature.description: Reported by OpenSSL (crypto/ec/asm/x25519-x86_64.pl) and BoringSSL (fiat-crypto MULX/ADX), not measured by this repository. Recorded so the citation cannot drift into reading as an AMA measurement (INVARIANT-36).
